title: A limit of constructibly closed subsets of spectral spaces along spectral maps is quasi-compact
statement: Let $(I,\le)$ be a preordered set (a set with a reflexive and transitive relation $\le$; no directedness is assumed), let $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ be spectral spaces [def-weil-spectral-space] and for $i\le i'$ let $f_{ii'}:X_{i'}\to X_i$ be spectral maps (continuous, with $f_{ii'}^{-1}(W)$ quasi-compact for every quasi-compact open $W\subseteq X_i$), with $f_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $f_{ii'}\circ f_{i'i''}=f_{ii''}$ for $i\le i'\le i''$. Let $X$ be a topological space with continuous maps $p_i:X\to X_i$, $f_{ii'}\circ p_{i'}=p_i$, which is a limit of the system in the category of topological spaces (the map $x\mapsto(p_i(x))_i$ is a bijection of $X$ onto $\{(x_i)\in\prod_iX_i: f_{ii'}(x_{i'})=x_i\text{ for }i\le i'\}$ and the topology of $X$ is the coarsest for which all $p_i$ are continuous). For each $i\in I$ let $Z_i\subseteq X_i$ be a subset which is closed in the constructible topology of $X_i$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-topology] (the topology on the set $X_i$ with subbase the quasi-compact open subsets of $X_i$ and their complements), such that $f_{ii'}(Z_{i'})\subseteq Z_i$ for all $i\le i'$. Then the subset $Z=\{x\in X: p_i(x)\in Z_i\text{ for all }i\in I\}$ of $X$ is quasi-compact in the topology induced from $X$: every covering of $Z$ by subsets open in $Z$ has a finite subcovering. In particular (taking $Z_i=X_i$ for all $i$) $X$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Topology, Lemma Tag 0A2V (label lemma-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces-quasi-compact, line 4779), parts (1) and (2), stated there for a diagram over any category; here for an inverse system over a preordered set. Stacks' limit lim Z_i (in topological spaces, of the subspaces Z_i) is the subspace Z of X: both are the compatible families with all components in the Z_i, with the coarsest topology making the maps to the X_i continuous. Stacks' proof uses Lemmas 0901 (lemma-constructible-hausdorff-quasi-compact), 005C (lemma-closed-in-quasi-compact), 08ZV (lemma-inverse-limit-quasi-compact) and the image of a quasi-compact space

proof.text: *Step 1 (the constructible topologies).* For $i\in I$ let $X_i'$ denote the set $X_i$ with its constructible topology [def-weil-pbc-constructible-topology]. Each $X_i'$ is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-constructible-topology-quasi-compact] and Hausdorff [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-constructible-topology-hausdorff], $X_i$ being spectral [def-weil-spectral-space]. For $i\le i'$ the map $f_{ii'}$ is spectral, hence continuous as a map $X_{i'}'\to X_i'$ [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-map-constructible-continuous]. By hypothesis $Z_i$ is closed in $X_i'$.

source.place: Topology, proof of Lemma Tag 0A2V (label lemma-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces-quasi-compact, line 4779), first three sentences (Lemmas 0901, 0A2S (1))

proof.text: *Step 2 (the constructible topology is finer).* For every $i$ the identity map $\iota_i:X_i'\to X_i$ is continuous. Indeed, let $U\subseteq X_i$ be open. Since $X_i$ is spectral [def-weil-spectral-space], the quasi-compact open subsets form a basis of its topology, so $U=\bigcup_\alpha U_\alpha$ with each $U_\alpha$ a quasi-compact open of $X_i$. Each $U_\alpha$ is a member of the subbase of the constructible topology [def-weil-pbc-constructible-topology], hence open in $X_i'$, and so is their union $U$.

source.place: Topology, paragraph after Definition Tag 08YG (definition-spectral-space), line 4300: 'the constructible topology is stronger than the given topology'; used in the proof of Lemma Tag 0A2V (line 4779), last two sentences

proof.text: *Step 3 (the product).* Let $P'=\prod_{i\in I}X_i'$ with the product topology, and $\mathrm{pr}_i:P'\to X_i'$ the projections, which are continuous (each $\mathrm{pr}_i^{-1}(V)$, $V\subseteq X_i'$ open, is a basic open set $\prod_jU_j$ with $U_i=V$ and $U_j=X_j'$ for $j\ne i$). By Step 1 and Tychonoff's theorem [lem-weil-pbc-tychonoff-product-quasi-compact] $P'$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Topology, proof of Lemma Tag 08ZV (label lemma-inverse-limit-quasi-compact, line 2475), used in the proof of Lemma Tag 0A2V (line 4779), first two sentences (Theorem Tag 08ZU)

proof.text: *Step 4 (the compatible families in the $Z_i$ form a closed subset).* Let $L=\{(x_i)\in P': x_i\in Z_i\text{ for all }i\in I,\ f_{ii'}(x_{i'})=x_i\text{ for all }i\le i'\}$. For $i\in I$ the set $\mathrm{pr}_i^{-1}(Z_i)$ is closed in $P'$, since $Z_i$ is closed in $X_i'$ (Step 1) and $\mathrm{pr}_i$ is continuous (its complement is $\mathrm{pr}_i^{-1}(X_i'\setminus Z_i)$, open). For $i\le i'$ the maps $f_{ii'}\circ\mathrm{pr}_{i'}$ and $\mathrm{pr}_i$ from $P'$ to $X_i'$ are continuous (Steps 1 and 3) and $X_i'$ is Hausdorff (Step 1), so $E_{ii'}=\{x\in P': f_{ii'}(\mathrm{pr}_{i'}(x))=\mathrm{pr}_i(x)\}$ is closed in $P'$ [lem-weil-pbc-hausdorff-equalizer-closed]. Hence $L=\bigcap_i\mathrm{pr}_i^{-1}(Z_i)\cap\bigcap_{i\le i'}E_{ii'}$, an intersection of closed subsets, is closed in $P'$.

source.place: Topology, proof of Lemma Tag 08ZV (label lemma-inverse-limit-quasi-compact, line 2475), used in the proof of Lemma Tag 0A2V (line 4779), third to last sentences (Stacks uses the closed graphs of Lemma Tag 08ZF, i.e. the diagonal criterion Tag 08ZE; the coincidence set used here is the same closed set), applied to the spaces $Z_i'$ as in the proof of Lemma Tag 0A2V

proof.text: *Step 5 ($L$ is quasi-compact).* By Steps 3 and 4, $L$ is a closed subset of the quasi-compact space $P'$, hence quasi-compact in the topology induced from $P'$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-in-quasi-compact].

source.place: Topology, proof of Lemma Tag 08ZV (label lemma-inverse-limit-quasi-compact, line 2475), used in the proof of Lemma Tag 0A2V (line 4779) (Lemma Tag 005C)

proof.text: *Step 6 (the map $\Phi:L\to X$ and its image).* Let $(x_i)\in L$. It is a compatible family ($f_{ii'}(x_{i'})=x_i$ for $i\le i'$), so by the hypothesis on $X$ there is exactly one $x\in X$ with $p_i(x)=x_i$ for all $i$; put $\Phi((x_i))=x$. Then $\Phi(L)=Z$: if $x=\Phi((x_i))$ then $p_i(x)=x_i\in Z_i$ for all $i$, so $x\in Z$; conversely, for $x\in Z$ the family $(p_i(x))_i$ lies in $L$ (its components lie in the $Z_i$, and $f_{ii'}(p_{i'}(x))=p_i(x)$ as $f_{ii'}\circ p_{i'}=p_i$), and $\Phi((p_i(x))_i)=x$ by uniqueness.

source.place: Topology, proof of Lemma Tag 0A2V (label lemma-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces-quasi-compact, line 4779): 'Z\' \to Z is a bijection on underlying sets' (limits of spaces have the limit of the underlying sets, Lemma Tag 08ZT (lemma-limits))

proof.text: *Step 7 ($\Phi$ is continuous).* Give $L$ the topology induced from $P'$. For every $i\in I$ we have $p_i\circ\Phi=\iota_i\circ\mathrm{pr}_i|_L$ as maps $L\to X_i$ (both send $(x_j)$ to $x_i$). This is continuous: $\mathrm{pr}_i|_L$ is the restriction to the subspace $L$ of the continuous map $\mathrm{pr}_i:P'\to X_i'$ (Step 3), and $\iota_i$ is continuous (Step 2). Since the topology of $X$ is the coarsest for which all $p_i$ are continuous, $\Phi:L\to X$ is continuous [lem-weil-pbc-initial-topology-continuity].

source.place: Topology, proof of Lemma Tag 0A2V (label lemma-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces-quasi-compact, line 4779): 'The maps Z\'_i \to Z_i are continuous, hence Z\' \to Z is continuous'

proof.text: *Step 8 (conclusion).* By Steps 5, 6 and 7, $Z=\Phi(L)$ is the image of the quasi-compact space $L$ under the continuous map $\Phi:L\to X$, hence $Z$ is quasi-compact in the topology induced from $X$ [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-image-quasi-compact]. For the last assertion take $Z_i=X_i$ for all $i$: $X_i$ is closed in $X_i'$, $f_{ii'}(X_{i'})\subseteq X_i$, and then $Z=X$, so $X$ is quasi-compact.
